dispatch.headline: The arcade fills up

image.alt: Tong Hui Kang, Dries Smit, Mark Barney, and Son Pham work on four small robots at an arcade bench. Dries is fitting a leg to his spider robot.
image.caption: Tong Hui Kang, Dries Smit, Mark Barney, and Son Pham at the arcade workbench.

sections.text:
Tong Hui Kang had the high score when the arcade opened. Vladislav Lavrentev slipped a thousandth ahead of Dries Smit for second, and the rest of Tuesday’s top ten barely had time to get comfortable. By Wednesday afternoon every one of those names was out of the top ten. Keith Tyser, absent from Tuesday evening’s board, was #1 and the only entrant above 0.400.

Salah Ibrahiemu went from twentieth to second. Lebxgue. came in third on the same displayed score. Akmal Azzam o'g'li and THIRUPATHI KANNAN K both climbed from outside Tuesday evening’s top fifty to round out the top five. The crowd behind them grew too. Kaggle showed 159 scored teams around this time on Tuesday and 304 on Wednesday.

sections.heading: Better runs, worse seats
sections.text:
Tong Hui Kang used to give ARC entrants a reason to refresh. When the queue backed up, Kaggle competitor mp sent readers to the tracker Tong built. Now it’s his name people look for. The solo entrant had nine scored submissions by Wednesday and beat his opening-day mark. He was down to twenty-fourth anyway.

Dries Smit put Tufa Labs on the board with a single scored entry on opening day. Now Kaggle shows seven scored entries and a higher score, good for thirty-ninth. Dries is still the only account listed under Dries @ Tufa Labs. Will Stefano Viel, Jeroen Cottaar, Isaiah Pressman, Michal Tešnar or Tommy He take a seat of their own?

The Kaggriculture crowd is moving too. Ahmed Berat Özer’s entry now goes by Pay-to-Compute. It sits eighteenth and lists Özer, Alperen Aydın and ulasdesouza. DECEM also improved and fell to eighty-second.

sections.heading: Jack builds from scratch

image.alt: Jack Cole wears a broad cyan visor while soldering a small copper robot in an arcade service booth.
image.caption: Jack Cole at his own bench.

sections.text:
Jack Cole went from fourth in Mark Barney’s Tuesday morning post to ninety-third on Wednesday’s board, even as his score edged up. The joint winner of the 2023 ARCathon told the Goose at launch that he was starting from scratch with an idea of his own. He was an adviser on Dries’s StochasticGoose when it won the ARC-AGI-3 Preview. They have separate entries in this arcade.

“I don’t expect this position to last long,” Barney had written when his entry was third. By Wednesday, he and Son Pham had improved their score and slipped to sixty-eighth under Logical Arbitrage. Barney publishes the Goose. Tyser competed alongside Barney and Pham on Team Turducken in ARC-AGI-3. Here Tyser has a separate, one-account entry, all the way at the top.

sections.heading: The game never waits
sections.text:
The cabinets in this arcade never wait. One offline agent gets a short brief, the screen, and a mouse and keyboard across 32 browser games. It might be lining up a jump while the platform has already moved. There’s $50,000 on the line and a final submission deadline of 1 March 2027.

The public board averages sixteen games, including the four teams can practice on. A separate sixteen decide who gets paid.
